newsitem.title: UK: British Airways cabin crews go on strike.
newsitem.headline: British Airways cabin crews go on strike.

text.p: Thousands of British Airways (BA) passengers faced disruption on Wednesday when cabin crews began the first of a series of three-day strikes, Britain's Sky television reported.

Members of the Transport and General Workers' Union (T&G) launched their strike at 6.00 a.m. (0500 GMT) despite a warning from BA that strikers would lose perks and face a lockout unless they promised to work normally in the future.
Sky said more than 150 BA flights from London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports would be hit by the walkout.

Britain's Press Association news agency said hopes of a breakthrough to the industrial dispute emerged overnight after talks between BA managers and union officials but it came too late to head off the strike.
The agency said there was an eerie silence at Heathrow's terminal one instead of the usual hurly-burly of the morning rush, with flight indicator boards showing few BA flights leaving for Europe.
The dispute arose over the airline's plans to save a billion pounds by the year 2000 through major restructuring. Earlier negotiations broke down on Sunday.
BA said its contingency plan, aimed at keeping as many flights running as possible, would go into action but admitted thousands of passengers may still be grounded.
